section_1.title: The Dimensional Paradox (0:00-0:45)
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a 1D line passing through every point of a 2D square. Clarify the prerequisite: mapping points between spaces. Use the intuition of 'infinite folding' to challenge the viewer's notion that a line cannot fill an area.
section_1.example: Visualizing a piece of string being folded infinitely until it covers the surface of a table.

section_2.title: The Peano Curve Construction (0:45-2:00)
section_2.content: Explain the iterative process. Start with a square divided into 9 smaller squares. Draw a path connecting their centers. Subdivide again to 81 squares, and refine the path. Emphasize self-similarity as the key to recursive scaling.
section_2.example: An animation showing a single line segment warping into a 'zigzag' that repeats at smaller scales until it occupies every pixel of a 3x3 grid.

section_3.title: The Hilbert Curve and Locality (2:00-3:30)
section_3.content: Introduce the Hilbert curve as a more efficient alternative to Peano. Explain the concept of 'Spatial Locality'—how the curve keeps points that are near each other in 2D space close to each other along the 1D path.
section_3.example: A digital camera sensor: Explain how a Hilbert curve scan helps the processor group nearby pixels together, improving image compression efficiency.

section_4.title: Real-World Applications (3:30-4:30)
section_4.content: Transition to practical uses. Discuss database indexing, memory mapping, and optimization. Show how reducing multidimensional data into a 1D sequence makes searching significantly faster.
section_4.example: A 'Robot Librarian' sorting books on a 2D grid: The robot follows a Hilbert path to retrieve books efficiently, minimizing travel time between similar categories.

section_5.title: Summary and Philosophical Conclusion (4:30-5:00)
section_5.content: Recap: Space-filling curves are not just mathematical curiosities, but tools to bridge the gap between human perception (2D/3D) and machine efficiency (1D strings).
section_5.example: A final visual overlay of a complex Hilbert curve morphing back into a simple straight line, symbolizing the elegance of mathematical reduction.
